name: Reproducible Notebooks and Pipelines
title: Reproducible Notebooks and Pipelines
answer: Reproducible notebooks and pipelines cover the practices that let a quantitative analysis be rerun by another person and produce the same result. They span the whole path from raw data through cleaning, modelling, and reporting, not just the final chart or table. Notebooks provide an interactive record of exploration, while pipelines provide an automated, parameterised way to execute the same steps at scale. The scope includes the environment, the data version, the code, and the decisions that connect them. A result is only reproducible when all of those parts are captured together.

sections.body: Reproducible notebooks and pipelines cover the practices that let a quantitative analysis be rerun by another person and produce the same result. They span the whole path from raw data through cleaning, modelling, and reporting, not just the final chart or table. Notebooks provide an interactive record of exploration, while pipelines provide an automated, parameterised way to execute the same steps at scale. The scope includes the environment, the data version, the code, and the decisions that connect them. A result is only reproducible when all of those parts are captured together.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: These workflows run on a mix of local machines, shared servers, and cloud notebook services. Pipelines typically execute on workflow engines, container runtimes, or job schedulers that can restart a failed step. Dependencies are pinned in environment files so that library versions do not drift between runs. Data lives in versioned object stores, databases, or file systems that record which snapshot was used. Compute may be CPU or GPU depending on the model, and the infrastructure must expose the same resources to every rerun.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The usual method is to explore in a notebook, then move stable logic into functions or scripts that a pipeline can call. Parameters are pulled out of the code, random seeds are fixed, and intermediate outputs are cached so that long steps do not need to be repeated. Tests compare a fresh run against a stored reference, allowing small numerical differences within a stated tolerance. The pipeline is then executed end to end from a clean environment to confirm that no hidden state remains. Documentation records the order of steps and the reason for each choice.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Governance for reproducible work centres on provenance, which means recording the data, code, parameters, and environment behind every result. Risks include hidden notebook state that changes results silently, credentials left in cells, and licences that restrict how data or code can be shared. Access control and audit trails help show who ran what and when. On this site, content links to the original paper rather than to a search tool, which keeps the chain of evidence visible. Clear attribution and licence checks are part of the same discipline.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward tighter coupling between interactive notebooks and automated pipelines, so that exploration can become production without a rewrite. Standards for describing computational steps and provenance metadata are maturing, which should make cross-platform reruns more common. Expect more automatic capture of environment and data versions at the moment a result is produced. As models grow, reproducibility will depend on recording model weights, training data snapshots, and evaluation settings alongside the analysis code. The boundary between a notebook and a pipeline is likely to become less important than the record they both leave behind.
